scope.carrier: English / Great Britain / company facilities when documented

confidence_policy.A: Full scholarly source text transcribing contemporaneous letter, precise original shelfmark; letter itself not inspected
confidence_policy.B: Voyage-level derived SlaveVoyages result publicly visible, official voyage ID but interactive original page not field-readable from this audit
confidence_policy.C: Academic chronology reproduced outside authorized book access; bibliographic publisher Project MUSE confirms book and appendix, but original source archive not inspected
confidence_policy.research_only: Do not plot until dated and place-located with sufficient independent basis; unresolved vessel identity and name variants documented separately
confidence_policy.B_2019_official_bulk: Official SlaveVoyages 2019 expanded CSV directly downloaded and checksum verified; recorded vessel/RESISTANCE code directly visible, but contemporaneous SOURCEA archival folios not read and database may have imputed year, flag and population.
confidence_policy.B_2020_official_compared: Official SlaveVoyages 2020 SPSS version directly downloaded with SHA256; 2019/2020 same edited research database family, so not an independent 17th-century contemporary written witness

case_records.location: James Fort / James Island (later Kunta Kinteh Island), Gambia River
case_records.casualty_source: RAC factor John Kastell letter Jan 24 1682 quoted in Eltis 2000 p.172
case_records.claim_limits: Numbers are the fort officer's retrospective account; the group of 105 was specifically male prisoners on 24 November. The 34 dead/40 wounded are from suppression at the trading fort, NOT shipboard middle-passage deaths; not to be added to voyage IMP deaths.
Secondary academic excerpt + voyage derivative, no original ship register; do not conflate this 1688 event with Taylor's separately dated 1689 Capt Osney entry before checking original chronology.

Only derived site presents readable numbers; 421-401 is a cross-field difference not verified death total; some secondary chronology writes Brome as vessel but derived voyage dataset lists captain John Brome and vessel America. Do not claim both are separate voyages.
238-186 is comparison not independent death ledger; chronological description gives ca.1696, voyage derivative says 1696 arrival. Source does not confirm precise day or latitude of uprising.

case_records.source_of_revolt_casualties: Eric Robert Taylor 2006 Appendix pp. 179-180 quotes Dow 1927 pp.79-84 and voyage 20173, text accessible on Studocu; original publisher Project MUSE paywalled
case_records.claim_limits: 28 people enslaved and 1 crewmember reported killed in a published academic bibliography's chronology are not to be combined with total 350 IMP middle-passage deaths as separate nonoverlapping losses. Neither is a list of individually identified persons.

research_only_candidates.name: Charles
research_only_candidates.warning: Official 2019 CSV confirms Charles (ID99009) as RESISTANCE=1, YEARAM1691, NATINIMP7, SLAXIMP179, SLAMIMP158, and SOURCEA=T70/17,26. Taylor's 17 killed is a separate scholarly claim unverified by original T70 folio. No exact revolt date or sea position; not yet in Atlas.

research_only_candidates.name: Dragon
research_only_candidates.warning: Museum publication directly supports 1699 Dragon revolt at African coast, but its captain, exact action date, boarded population, 7+2 alleged dead, and original sources remain unresolved. Cannot infer deaths from 14 belonging to owners on arrival. Not included in the 2019/2020 14-code sample and must not be added to its numerator as if present in dataset.
research_only_candidates.bristol_museum_description: Topsham voyage in 1699; enslaved people rebelled on board while off African coast; original Topsham owners' share recorded as 14 enslaved people upon Caribbean arrival after another RAC factor placed additional people aboard; museum says cargo originally valued GBP400 (not adjusted to 2026).
competing_captain_attributions: Henry Taylor (secondary Taylor 2006 Appendix citing Tattersfield 1991)
Christopher Butcher (another trade-ports historical note citing Tattersfield 1991)

audit_guards: 1688 Calabar shore attack not within ship
1693/1696 embarked minus disembarked not inherently deaths
1699 Albion 350 IMP not 28 revolt death, no summing 28+350
No vessel track, territorial polygons or measured British land area
Official 2019 bulk CSV establishes *coded* resistance for 14 Great Britain flagged records, NOT total uprising prevalence; 1689 Osney potential duplication remains.
2019 and 2020 are successive formats from same historiographical database, not independent original witnesses; 2020 SOURCEA can truncate citations.
Dragon 1699 uprising attested by Bristol Museums, despite absent in 14 code sample, so NEVER claim sample exhausts 17th-century resistance.
1699 Jamaica law authorized monthly fees plus booty, not proof of actual total spending; map via existing Spanish Town administrative reference E091.
